en: Sure thing, good to meet ya!
Right, time to put in another hard day's work.
You work hard at your job too, eh?
, it's you. Morning!
note: After the name: '{NAME}, it's you. Morning!' (as #101/#1784).

en: You're a steady one, always up early.
I'm off to buy in meat myself. See ya.
Morning! Lovely morning, eh?
Fine weather puts me in a good mood all day.
You're never too lively in the mornings, eh?
You're up early, but I reckon you're
really not a morning person. Well, chin up.
Oh, evening.
What's up, mate? Lost your way?
You don't look like you're from around here.
Yes. I have only just come to London.
But I am not lost.
Oh, I see, I see. Sorry, I jumped the gun.
note: Msg 202257 joins #4977 on the same line: variant with a trailing space.

variants.en: Oh, I see, I see. Sorry, I jumped the gun.

en: It's dark around here, so watch yourself.
Hey, hold on, at least tell me your name.
We're in the same city. We'll meet again.
I'm Malcolm, the butcher.
Well then...
Right, get home safe.
, it's you. Hey!
note: After the name: '{NAME}, it's you. Hey!' (as #1784).

en: Out here in those fancy clothes again?
You must be real carefree or real gutsy.
Lots of workers round here. Some of 'em
note: Sentence runs over #4987/#4988 (shared with msg 202350, where #5059 replaces this row).

en: can't stand even seeing a man of good family
walk by. Don't come here much at night.
Hey, it's you. We meet again.
There's been some nasty business, so go easy
on the night walks.
Mind you, Jack the Ripper's
victims are all women, from what I hear.
If you get in trouble, shout for help.
Welcome, come on in!
What'll you have? Plenty of fresh meat here.
This is... a butcher's?
Well, well, what's this fella on about?
A tailor's with slabs of meat hanging up?
There's no such thing in this world!
I'm Malcolm, the owner. Order what you like.
I'll cut it to whatever size you want.
I see...
I smelled blood and couldn't help coming in.
(Oops, I let that slip.)
Ha ha, you've got quite a nose on you.
Well, no meat's cut without bleeding.
You'll have to put up with the smell.
Look, I went and cut my own hand just now.
Didn't get any on the goods, so don't worry.
Is that so...
Well, you should be careful.
Oh, it's you! I've been waiting for ya.
What'll it be? Got plenty of fresh meat.
I can't help noticing the smell of blood.
What, don't you want any meat?
Welcome!
How about some meat for supper?
You've got a missus at least, right?
No, I'm afraid I live alone.
What? That's pitiful.
A ladies' man like you, still single?
You never buy meat, yet you come by a lot.
Got nobody who'll cook for you?
Poor fella. Why not come round my place?
My wife's a great cook.
Drop by sometime if you feel like it.
Oh, come on in.
I bet you're not buying anything, but fine.
Have a browse all the same.
Drop by my house too, I don't mind.
It's just round the corner from the shop.
Hey, what's up, mate?
Yeah, good to meet ya!
Oh, it's you.
Come by the shop and I'll give you a deal!
, it's you. What's up?
The butcher's isn't open right now.
As you can probably see.
